key_insight: Long-range ML interatomic potentials better capture Coulomb-driven defect energetics in SrTiO$_3$ than short-range models, especially as vacancy separation increases.
engineering_relevance: Accurate long-range defect modeling can improve predictive simulations of oxide reliability, diffusion, and defect-mediated transport in functional ceramics.
method: Benchmark four MLIPs: short-range MACE vs. long-range MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES, and LOREM.
Test first on synthetic point-charge systems, then on DFT data for SrTiO$_3$ with Sr--O Schottky vacancy pairs.
Evaluate oxygen-vacancy migration barriers with CI-NEB and molecular dynamics as a function of vacancy-pair separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a staged benchmark from idealized electrostatics to first-principles SrTiO$_3$ defect calculations, specifically probing how well each model reproduces long-range interaction effects and migration barriers.
watch_item: DFT total energies mix electrostatics with screening and exchange-correlation effects, so performance on defect energetics may not map cleanly to pure Coulomb accuracy.
paper_title: Long-Range Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Defect Energetics in SrTiO$_3$
